lines.text: Sarah wants eggs next Friday. On signet, that's a futures contract — a Cashu future.
Each production day is its own series. The unit names the farm, the commodity, and the maturity. Friday's eggs are not Saturday's eggs.
The terms are a small signed document. Its SHA-256 digest is its address. Every proof's secret carries one tag pointing at it — future, version one, that address.
Sarah opens the farm tab and picks a production day.
Five eggs, at twenty-one sats each.
One hundred and five sats. A real Lightning invoice on signet.
Paid. The mint issues exactly five claims, locked to Sarah's wallet key.
Five bearer claims, and the details show the unit, the terms digest, and the maturity.
The farm's ledger counts totals only — five issued, capacity ten thousand. A claim beyond capacity simply cannot be minted.
Plans change. Sarah sends two claims to Bob.
The swap keeps the unit and the future tag, and mints fresh secrets. What leaves is a bearer token — the farm never learns who holds it.
Sarah keeps three.
Bob's phone. He pastes the token.
Two claims, now Bob's. The farm's ledger never moved — total supply is still five.
Friday, four p.m. — the series matures. For the film, we advance the clock with the admin override.
Bob redeems two at the counter.
The wallet burns the proofs and shows the teller a code.
The operator matches the code, hands over two eggs, and settles. Until that moment, nothing is consumed.
Redeemed. Two claims burned, two eggs delivered — and the spent proofs can never be spent again.
Signet sats in. Dated bearer claims out. Hand to hand, no registry. Physical redemption at maturity.
NUT-32, draft one — live on signet, enforced by the mint, and checked end to end by automated tests.
